summary:
Legacy payment infrastructure may still function, but hidden costs from false declines, outages, fraud and manual processes are making modernisation a strategic priority for banks.
The post Legacy Is No Longer Cheap. The Economics of Payments Modernisation. appeared first on The Fintech Times.
content: Legacy payment infrastructure may continue to function for banks, but hidden costs are shifting industry priorities. Issues such as false declines, unexpected outages, rising fraud, and inefficient manual processes are driving financial institutions to view payments modernisation as a critical strategic priority. Maintaining older systems is proving to be increasingly expensive, making a transition to modern alternatives essential for long-term operational success.

title: Why payment systems matter for sustainable consumption
summary: A strong shift toward sustainable consumption is arguably one of the most impactful things that can ...
content: Payment systems play a crucial role in enabling and accelerating the shift toward sustainable consumption.
